item.title: Coal front: The Tipline for 26 February 2026
item.description: Vanguard is the first asset manager to settle Texas-led claims of an anti-coal conspiracy. “Coal is an essential industry to support America’s ever-growing energy demands, and my office will continue to uproot and destroy any attempt by investment giants to push a woke agenda that puts American energy at risk,” said Texas attorney general Ken Paxton in a statement on Thursday. item.title: Wall Street accused of using Kirkland to “punish” Optimum
item.description: Asset managers including JPMorgan, Apollo Global Management and BlackRock “bullied” Kirkland & Ellis into dropping Optimum as a client, the telecommunications company has alleged.

item.title: Netflix walks away from Warner Bros deal
item.description: Netflix has abandoned its pursuit of Warner Bros hours after Paramount submitted a superior offer.

item.title: Ferguson: “No political antitrust problem at FTC”
item.description: Federal Trade Commission Chair Andrew Ferguson has rejected claims that antitrust enforcement has become overtly political during his tenure, stating those concerns have been “mostly generated by the press”.

item.title: By committee: The Briefing for 27 February 2026
item.description: Despite the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority almost doubling its staff over the past decade, the economy’s “competitive dynamics” have deteriorated, according to the chair of an influential parliamentary committee. Additionally, Liam Byrne MP took aim at the agency’s enforcement record and readiness to launch market probes to address “spiralling” cost-of-living pressures. Also in The Briefin...

item.title: Law firms call for overhaul of CMA’s efficiencies approach
item.description: Paul Weiss Rifkind Wharton & Garrison, Slaughter and May, Norton Rose Fulbright and 17 other leading law firms have urged the UK’s Competition and Markets Authority to fundamentally alter its approach to assessing merger efficiencies arguments.

item.title: Belgium launches Google Adtech probe
item.description: Ongoing uncertainty about potential remedies in US and EU cases targeting Google’s adtech business helped justify a newly announced antitrust investigation by the Belgian Competition Authority into the company, its lead investigator has revealed.

item.title: Down to the wire: The Tipline for 27 February 2026
item.description: Charter and Cox Enterprises have received regulatory approval for their $34.5 billion tie-up to create a cable and broadband giant. item.title: DOJ backs patent holders’ ability to seek injunction
item.description: Non-practising patent holders can demonstrate the need for a permanent injunction prohibiting future infringement, the Department of Justice has said, further cementing the Antitrust Division’s embrace of stronger intellectual property protections.

item.title: Five firms guide Paramount on blockbuster Warner Bros deal
item.description: Paramount utilised at least five law firms to help push for clearance of its $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros, as Democrats lined up behind state enforcers in hopes of blocking the deal.
